clue.text: Father recalled son having brief panic, facing wide London street once

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for father

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word son is taken backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym for panic is dropped

parts.note: panic is terror
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A dad reminisces about his son's moment of fright on a broad old London thoroughfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns SON into NOS; 'brief' trims TERROR to TERRO. Paternoster Row, by St Paul's Cathedral, was the centre of London's book trade until the Blitz destroyed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternoster Row was a real City of London street, largely destroyed by bombing in 1940, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Cassette or CD player for each child too, getting wrapped short time before

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head
a son is a child

indicators.note: the word for too is wrapped around the next pieces, which sit inside it

parts.note: too means also, in addition
T is the abbreviation for time, shortened
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A parent buys a music player for each child as well, just before a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting wrapped' means the synonym for too opens up to hold the short time and the old word for before; the definition dates the clue to the Walkman era.
explanation.definitionFit: A Walkman-style portable music device for one listener with headphones played cassettes or discs.

clue.text: Courier's one with a kind side

parts.note: a kind or sort is a type
a face is a side, as of a cube or cliff

explanation.surface: A delivery rider is described as a pleasant person with a gentle disposition.
explanation.walkthrough: Courier is the typewriter-style font, not a delivery person; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Courier is one particular font design, so it is an example of this lettering style.

clue.text: New hairdo: initially cut, then set

indicators.note: new signals the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement
the first letter of the word hairdo is cut away

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: At the salon a fresh hairstyle is first trimmed and then set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially cut' removes the H of HAIRDO, leaving AIRDO, which 'New' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is called a set, as in a television or wireless set.

clue.text: Our starter (takeaway) contains nothing sinister

indicators.note: the starter of the word Our is its opening letter
contains says the next word's synonym holds the zero inside it

parts.note: takeaway in arithmetic is subtraction, minus
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A takeaway meal starter that turns out to contain nothing seems a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takeaway' is not food here but subtraction, MINUS; O goes inside it, after the O from 'Our starter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening or foreboding is sinister, giving warning of harm to come.

clue.text: Taught after time out 11

parts.note: 11 across is OFF COLOUR, so read 'out off colour': off shuffles the word out to UTO, and colour gives RED

explanation.surface: A teacher recalls having taught a class after time off, ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Substitute the answer to 11 across: 'out off colour' gives an anagram of OUT ('off') followed by a colour, RED, all after T.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach or instruct someone privately is to have taught them.

clue.text: Unusual soil element in each half of divided land?

definitions.text: element in each half of divided land?

parts.note: unusual means rare
soil is earth

explanation.surface: A curious soil component found in both halves of a partitioned country.
explanation.walkthrough: Split LAND as LA and ND: lanthanum and neodymium are both lanthanide elements, so each half of the divided word is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanthanum (La) and neodymium (Nd) belong to the lanthanide group of metals collectively given this name.

clue.text: See 1
If this is pulled on, you're probably in the wrong jacket

definitions.text: If this is pulled on, you're probably in the wrong jacket

parts.words: If this is pulled on, you're probably in the wrong jacket
parts.note: the word is both a short sailor's double-breasted jacket and a cannabis cigarette; you pull on (draw on) the smoke, but you pull on a jacket, so the one you drag on is the wrong kind of jacket

explanation.surface: A fashion warning that anything you tug on may mean you have the wrong coat on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled on' suggests putting clothing on, but here it means inhaling from a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a reefer jacket worn by sailors and a hand-rolled cannabis joint that one draws on.

clue.text: Wantonly lay 9 women, if one's not truly married

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly, without restraint, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the numeral 9 is spelt out as the word nine, not the 9 across answer

explanation.surface: A rake boasts of seducing nine women, so his marriage is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a cross-reference to 9 across but is just the number nine, spelt out as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse in a purely formal union, with no real marital relationship, is a partner by title alone.

clue.text: Speedy attack with a little pace injected

indicators.note: injected says the small piece is put inside the attack word

parts.note: a raid is an attack

indicators.note: a little of the word pace is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A quick assault succeeds because a little extra pace was added.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and quick are synonyms describing fast movement.

clue.text: Contents of 9 are left out, as blank page added

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inner letters, the outer ones dropped

parts.note: the numeral read as the word nine

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The insides of a nine-page booklet have been removed, with blank sheets put in.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' again means the word NINE, whose contents are IN; 'out' rearranges ARE LEFT to TERLEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank sheet bound between the printed leaves of a book is an inserted interleaving page.

clue.text: Football club told strips in Round Four must be kind of blue?

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in says the club and the stripped word are placed inside round and four
strips means removes the outer layer, so only the middle of told is kept

explanation.surface: A football club's strips in round four have to be some shade of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strips' looks like football kit but is the instruction to peel the outer letters off 'told'; 'in' places those pieces after the F of FOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are risqué; humour that is indecent or in poor taste is said to be this, so it is one kind of blue.

clue.text: Fragrant resinous substance ratel emits when short of cover

indicators.note: with its cover stripped off, the phrase ratel emits shows the letters held within it

explanation.surface: A honey badger lets off a sweet-smelling resin when it lacks shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A ratel is a honey badger, which really does emit a strong smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Confrontationally attacks account charges

parts.note: charges are costs

explanation.surface: A customer angrily challenges the fees on a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach and challenge someone aggressively is to accost them, a hostile verbal attack.

clue.text: Something very funny about 4's topping, a fermented dairy product

indicators.note: about says the funny word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a scream is something hilarious
the top of clue 4 is its first word, Our

explanation.surface: A hilarious bit of fun about a cheese topping made from fermented milk.
explanation.walkthrough: '4's topping' means the first word of clue 4's text, not the start of its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream soured by lactic acid bacteria is a cultured dairy food used in dips and on potatoes.

clue.text: Fuel used by older vans

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Older delivery vans tend to run on diesel.
explanation.walkthrough: Derv, from diesel-engined road vehicle, is the British name for diesel fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel for road vehicles is a fuel, known in Britain by this acronym.

clue.text: Deviant youth leader in foreign capital

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
foreign means strange, alien, so the letters are made unfamiliar
the leader of the word youth is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A wayward youth heads up a gang in some overseas capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts Y inside the anagram of CAPITAL, giving A-T-Y-PICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant means departing from the norm, which is unusual or not typical.

clue.text: See 8
Baby, uttering repeated pleadings at first, gets to bring 22

indicators.note: at first says the opening letters of the preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: A baby's repeated cries finally produce the expected result.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is UPWIND, so the definition reads 'bring up wind', as one does after feeding a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing trapped air from the stomach through the mouth is bringing up wind, a belch.

clue.text: Parade errand boy in front of social worker

indicators.note: in front of places the errand boy word before the worker word

parts.note: a page is a boy employed to run errands, as in a hotel
the ant is a social insect, and workers are a caste of ants

explanation.surface: A messenger boy walks at the head of a procession ahead of a care worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a care professional, but means an insect from a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession or spectacle with costumes and floats is a type of public show or display.

clue.text: What's wife left out? It needs around two small pinches of marjoram or sage

indicators.note: around says the pinched herb letters go on both sides of the other piece
two says the pinch is taken twice

parts.note: a small pinch of the word marjoram is its first two letters

indicators.note: left out says the wife letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A cook wonders what to do without the wife's help, adding pinches of marjoram or sage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sage' looks like the herb with marjoram but means a wise man: HAT from WHAT, wrapped by MA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A title given to a revered wise person in India, most famously Gandhi.

clue.text: Dramatist setting story in Rome, surprisingly

indicators.note: in says the story word is set inside the reordered city
surprisingly hints at an unexpected order for these letters

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib

explanation.surface: A playwright sets a tale in the Italian capital, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' reorders Rome as MORE, which is then split to take the story inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventeenth-century French comic playwright of Tartuffe is a famous writer for the stage.

clue.text: See 1
Victory in FA Trophy? "Header's missed at the death", reported into the blower

indicators.note: the header of the phrase is its first letter, which is left out

parts.note: the FA Trophy is a cup competition in English non-league football
a victory is a win

indicators.note: at the death means at the very end, so the last letter of reported is used

explanation.surface: A cup-final report: the decisive header missed in the dying seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The blower is British slang for the telephone, but here it is the wind that blows; 'at the death' is a football phrase for the last moments.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading against the direction the wind blows from is moving into the wind.

clue.text: Theme best served cold? Not half!

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, the second half dropped

parts.note: food served cold is iced

explanation.surface: A nod to the saying that revenge is a dish best served cold, answered with 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but here it halves ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion or study is a theme.

clue.text: Dizzy spell? 11, with eg staggers

indicators.note: staggers means reels, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the number 11 written as two ones, the Roman numerals I and I

explanation.surface: A dizzy spell: someone feels ill and staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to 11 across (meaning ill) but is two ones, II; the anagram of SPELL, II and EG gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizzy Gillespie was the American jazz trumpeter, so his nickname stands for his surname.

clue.text: One that's still smouldering, as three months come to an end

definitions.meaning: a glowing remnant of coal or wood in a dying fire

definitions.text: three months come to an end
definitions.meaning: September, November and December each end with these five letters

explanation.surface: A last coal still glowing as autumn and winter months draw to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a fire's ashes keeps smouldering after the flames die.

clue.text: Repeat has said writer worried

indicators.note: said says the word writer is spoken, and the spelling is a different one with that sound

parts.note: taken as written, spoken aloud
ate means worried, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A repeated broadcast has an author fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: REITER is a German cavalryman, pronounced like 'writer'; ATE is worried in the sense of 'what's eating you?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To say again or do over is to repeat.

clue.text: Painter content to redaub a Constable

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: An artist happily repaints a Constable landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like willing but means the contents of 'redaub a Constable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was the twentieth-century Irish-born figurative artist, so this is a painter's surname.

clue.text: "I'm Tory", hollered eccentric former drag artist

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A former female impersonator loudly declares his Conservative loyalties.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Riley was a music-hall and film character, an Irish washerwoman played in drag by Arthur Lucan.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Lucan's washerwoman act was a famous drag role of the 1930s to 1950s variety stage and screen.
